target.value_note: Approximately 4.3 V is a supplied requirement, not a measurement; neither reference electrode nor full-cell terminal voltage is specified.

candidate_list_provenance.reason: Proposed comparison set; the issue supplied no candidate identities. Chemical structures, stereochemistry and lots remain unverified.

candidates.name: ethylene carbonate
candidates.assessment: Useful comparator for graphite interphase formation; not a universal high-voltage choice, especially for Ni-rich cathodes.

candidates.name: ethyl methyl carbonate
candidates.assessment: Compare EC-containing baseline and, conditionally for Ni-rich/graphite cells, an EC-free formulation with a validated interphase-forming additive.

candidates.name: dimethyl carbonate
candidates.assessment: Relevant in both carbonate and sulfolane mixtures; mixture/salt evidence cannot be assigned to the isolated molecule.

candidates.name: propylene carbonate
candidates.assessment: Poor graphite interphase compatibility in conventional formulations is a constraint; not a blanket rejection across all additives, salts and concentrations.

candidates.name: sulfolane
candidates.assessment: Promising high-voltage formulation lead, but salt/additive-dependent graphite behavior, transport and wetting prevent selection on oxidative stability alone.

candidates.name: fluoroethylene carbonate
candidates.role: interphase-forming additive comparator, not neat-solvent winner
candidates.assessment: Evaluate as an additive within a complete formulation; beneficial sacrificial reduction is not equivalent to intrinsic reductive stability.

engineering_proposal.note: Research priorities only. No total ranking, solvent mixture recipe or voltage approval is established.
